title: Best Air Fryers UK
short: Single-drawer, dual-drawer and oven-style air fryers compared by capacity, power and who they suit.
intro: Air fryers now range from compact single baskets to dual-drawer machines that cook a full meal at once. This guide compares models tested by Expert Reviews (chips, hash browns, whole chicken and energy-use tests on more than 30 air fryers) and by Mumsnet's product testers in real family kitchens, so you can match capacity, features and budget to how you actually cook.

products.name: 5000 Series Dual Basket Steam Air Fryer NA555/09
products.best_for: Households that want the best results and are happy to learn the controls
products.summary: Expert Reviews named this its 2026 Air Fryer of the Year. It pairs two baskets with a steaming function, plus a self-cleaning mode, which makes it more versatile than a standard air fryer.
pros: Excellent cooking results in independent testing
products.search: Philips 5000 Series Dual Basket Steam Air Fryer NA555/09

products.name: Foodi Dual Zone AF300UK
products.best_for: Families who want two independent zones and proven results
products.summary: A long-standing favourite. Sync and match features let you finish two different foods at the same time, and reviewers rate the cooking results highly.
cons: Limited total capacity for large households

products.name: Foodi Max Dual Zone AF400UK
products.best_for: Bigger households that need generous capacity in two drawers
products.summary: Mumsnet's best overall and best dual air fryer. Its tester found the 9.5L split across two generous drawers gave a family of four room for a main and a side, the sync function brought both to the finish together, and the chips were the crispiest she had made in an air fryer. The main drawbacks are the price and the lack of viewing windows.
pros: Dual drawers with mix, match and sync programmes
cons: Pricey, though Mumsnet says it offers good long-term value
products.search: Ninja Foodi Max Dual Zone AF400UK

products.name: Vortex Plus Dual Drawer
products.best_for: Buyers who want a dual-drawer machine without the top-tier price
products.summary: Expert Reviews' best mid-range air fryer and Mumsnet's best for chips. Clear windows with interior lights let you check food without opening a drawer, and Mumsnet's tester got consistently strong results with homemade and frozen chips and roast potatoes. At 7.6L it suits a household of around three better than a large family; Mumsnet notes availability is limited.
cons: 7.6L can feel tight for larger families
products.search: Instant Vortex Plus Dual Drawer air fryer

products.name: Double Stack XL SL400UK
products.best_for: Anyone short on counter space who still wants big capacity
products.summary: Expert Reviews' pick for smaller kitchens and Mumsnet's best dual air fryer for small kitchens. The drawers stack vertically, so it takes far less worktop width than side-by-side designs while still offering 9.5L and up to four layers of food. It is deep front-to-back, so measure first.
pros: Can cook four layers of food at once
cons: Some owners report uneven cooking, though Mumsnet's tester didn't experience it
products.search: Ninja Double Stack XL SL400UK air fryer

products.name: Air Fryer Max Pro AF180UK
products.best_for: Single-drawer buyers who cook a lot of frozen chips and snacks
products.summary: A single-drawer model with a Max Crisp mode up to 240°C, which is well suited to crisping frozen food quickly.
products.search: Ninja Air Fryer Max Pro AF180UK

products.name: Foodi FlexDrawer AF500UK
products.best_for: Cooks who want one huge drawer for a Sunday roast or two smaller ones
products.summary: A flexible drawer that works as one large cooking space or as two zones, giving excellent results for large joints.
cons: Drawer is too large for most dishwashers

products.name: AirTwin XXL
products.best_for: Buyers who want to avoid PFAS non-stick coatings
products.summary: Expert Reviews highlights its non-stick coating as free from PFAS, which is a deciding factor for buyers who want to avoid so-called forever chemicals.

products.name: Air Fryer 5.5L
products.best_for: Couples and small households who want a single, good-value air fryer
products.summary: Mumsnet's panel picked this as its budget option. It has a medium-sized basket, 11 presets and a dishwasher-safe basket, and delivers excellent results for the price.
cons: Basket is tricky to hand wash

products.name: Dual Blaze Twinfry
products.best_for: Households that want to switch between one large drawer and two zones
products.summary: Mumsnet's most versatile pick converts between a dual-zone and single-zone layout, with sync and match features and app connectivity.
pros: Converts between dual and single zone
cons: Main basket is awkward to hand wash
products.search: Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry air fryer

products.name: Tri Zone 13.6L Air Fryer & Oven
products.best_for: Big households that want three foods cooked independently
products.summary: A very large air fryer and oven with three independent zones and good build quality. Mumsnet's testers found it good value, though it is bulky and noisy.
cons: Opening one zone pauses all three
products.search: Cuisinart Tri Zone 13.6L Air Fryer Oven

products.name: AIRX AI 5L Digital Air Fryer
products.best_for: One or two people who want smart features without premium pricing
products.summary: Mumsnet's best smart air fryer. Its AI mode analyses the food load and adjusts time and heat, though the tester found it worked best with straightforward batches rather than mixed ingredients. Quiet running, a slim shape and good results were the bigger everyday wins, but 5L felt cramped for a family of four.
pros: AI cooking is an interesting extra at this price
cons: 5L is tight for a family of four

products.name: CRISPi Portable Air Fryer
products.best_for: One or two people, meal prep, or a compact second appliance
products.key_spec: Glass containers up to 3.8L, four modes
products.summary: Mumsnet's best small air fryer swaps the usual drawer for two borosilicate-glass containers (around 3.8L and 1.4L) under a removable heating pod, so you can watch food cook and store leftovers with the included lids. It needs more turning than a drawer model and has no manual temperature control.
pros: Glass containers, with no plastic touching the food
Two container sizes suit small meals and meal prep
cons: Too small for most family dinners
Needs more flipping than a drawer model

products.name: Foodi MAX Health Grill & Air Fryer AG551UK
products.best_for: Households that grill a lot of meat and fish
products.summary: Mumsnet's best air fryer grill combines a roomy grill, a 5.7L cooking pot and a 3.8L crisper basket with an integrated meat probe. The tester found the controls easy, particularly for steak, chicken and fish, but it is very large and Mumsnet advises buying it for the grill and probe rather than for chips.
cons: Interior is harder to clean than a standard basket
products.search: Ninja Foodi MAX Health Grill Air Fryer AG551UK

products.name: Dual Basket Air Fryer 8L
products.best_for: Buyers who want two baskets at a modest price
products.summary: Mumsnet's best-value dual-basket model. It has viewing windows with internal lights, sync (but no match) and strong cooking results, but the baskets must be washed by hand. Mumsnet notes the tested 8L model has been discontinued, so check the current version.

guide.q: What size air fryer do I need?
guide.a: As a rough guide, 3-4L suits one or two people, 4-5.5L suits smaller households, and 7-10L (often split across two drawers) suits families or anyone who wants to cook a main and a side at the same time. Measure your worktop, including depth, before you buy.

guide.q: Are dual-drawer air fryers worth it?
guide.a: They let you cook two different foods at once, and most have a sync mode so both finish together. The trade-off is a bigger footprint and a higher price, so they make most sense for families and regular batch cooks.

guide.q: Do air fryers use less energy than an oven?
guide.a: Air fryers heat a much smaller space, so for small and medium portions they typically use less energy than a full-size oven. Energy use varies by model, so check independent test results if running cost matters to you.

guide.q: What does PFAS-free mean on an air fryer?
guide.a: PFAS are a group of synthetic chemicals sometimes used in non-stick coatings. Some manufacturers now advertise PFAS-free coatings. Check the product listing if this matters to you.
